summary: Phase 3 Workspace AI Licensing & Revenue Share tested end-to-end (backend + web). 16/16 pytest cases pass covering billing-rules defaults, RBAC (owner/admin, super-admin), consent preview, enable idempotency, patch, disable, workspace/creator/admin ledger math (base + per_user*active_users, 30% platform, 70% creator, TeamNest-owned keeps 100%), and PUT rules auto-adjust of creator_revenue_percent. Web UI: /workspace-ai renders correctly for super admin (all 3 tabs), nav link hidden for members, rules-save toast confirms PUT works. Two minor issues to flag; core module is solid.

minor.issue: Any authenticated user (even a plain member) can read the global revenue-share rules. Fee schedule is not particularly sensitive but consider gating to owner/admin/super_admin for consistency with the rest of the module.

ui_bugs.issue: Non-privileged members who type /workspace-ai directly still load the page; API 403s show TWO 'Failed to load workspace AI' error toasts (each API call fires its own). Sidebar link is correctly hidden, but the route itself has no client-side RBAC guard.

Dropdown offers 'Selected departments/roles/users' but there is no follow-up picker in the modal to actually choose department/role/user IDs — enable posts with empty enabled_departments/enabled_roles/enabled_users arrays, making non-workspace scopes effectively no-ops.

issues: Two identical error toasts stacked when a member hits /workspace-ai (Promise.all fires 3 requests, 2 fail → catch shows toast twice due to shared handler)

action_items: Add client-side RBAC guard on /workspace-ai route (redirect non owner/admin/super_admin to /chats) OR at minimum render an inline 'You don't have access' state instead of double error toasts.
Fix the double 'Failed to load workspace AI' toast — the shared load() catches every failing request separately in Promise.all; dedupe or show a single toast.
Implement the department/role/user picker in EnableModal when availability_scope !== 'workspace', or hide the non-workspace options until the picker is built.
(Optional) Gate GET /api/workspace-ai/billing-rules behind owner/admin for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: services/ai_employee_billing.py compute_deployment_billing: uses `dep.get('base_monthly_fee') or rules['min_builder_fee']` — a legitimate 0 override would fall back to the min fee. Consider `dep['base_monthly_fee'] if dep.get('base_monthly_fee') is not None else rules['min_builder_fee']` (same for per_user_monthly_fee/platform_fee_percent). The enable endpoint already uses this correct pattern; the compute path is inconsistent.

routes/workspace_ai.py PATCH /workspace-ai/employees/{eid}: writes None into base_monthly_fee/per_user_monthly_fee/platform_fee_percent if the caller omits them (because DeployConfig defaults them to None). This can silently zero out or reset custom pricing on a PATCH intended to change scope only. Use exclude_unset in the request model or drop None-valued fields before $set.

routes/workspace_ai.py `_owner_only` grants access based on the caller's role in ANY workspace they own — e.g. buildertest@ is `owner` of their own tiny workspace and therefore passes owner-only checks against a shared endpoint. Role check should be re-derived from current['workspace_id'] context rather than the JWT's cached role.
